chunks: "There is no Eid for the Muslims, whether Eid al-Adha or Eid al-Fitr, except that grief is renewed therein for the family of Muhammad."
It was said: "And why is that?"
He said: "Because they see their right in the hands of others."

key_terms.أَضْحًى: Eid al-Adha, the festival of sacrifice
key_terms.عِيدٍ: festival day observed by the Muslims
key_terms.فِطْرٍ: Eid al-Fitr, the festival marking the end of fasting
key_terms.لِآلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: for the family of Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, i.e. the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: Why do Eid al-Adha and Eid al-Fitr renew grief for the Ahl al-Bayt?
ai.summary: Imam Muhammad al-Baqir عليه السلام states that the major Muslim festivals renew sorrow for the Ahl al-Bayt because those occasions highlight that their rightful authority is held by others. The hadith expresses the grief of Āl Muḥammad عليهم السلام in connection with usurped right and leadership.
